Job Description

Are you passionate about making a tangible impact and want to tackle real-world challenges where sustainability meets profit?

Join Grundfos as a Senior Manager in our Group Strategy function and embark on our journey to become the leading provider of intelligent water and climate solutions globally!

This is a highly attractive opportunity for a seasoned strategy and M&A professional with 6+ years of experience - ideally gained in a top-tier consultancy or a dynamic corporate environment. The role is a perfect platform to accelerate your career further in a purpose-driven and globally impactful company.

What is the job about?

As a Senior Manager in Group Strategy, you will lead projects in both our strategic M&A team and our in-house corporate consulting team and. You will report to the Director, Strategic Growth Platforms, and collaborate with 25 highly skilled colleagues from more than 10 nationalities and diverse professional backgrounds - including long-term Grundfos specialists, former top-tier consultants, and alumni of the Grundfos Global Graduate Programme.

Together, we solve key challenges at the top of the C-suite agenda, ensuring Grundfos remains at the forefront of innovation, sustainability, and social impact.

Furthermore, you will:

• 
Lead and contribute to strategic projects across the entire Grundfos organisation in areas such as M&A (Pre-DD & CDD), corporate strategy, and growth initiatives.

• 
Take full ownership of project delivery from scoping and planning through execution - ensuring timely results that align with organisational priorities.

• 
Engage and manage a broad range of stakeholders, including senior executives, functional leaders, and cross-disciplinary teams across sales, business development, operations, and engineering.

• 
Translate strategic ambitions into actionable roadmaps and measurable outcomes, ensuring buy-in and accountability across the business.

• 
Build strong internal relations and networks while continuously developing your project leadership, stakeholder management, and consulting capabilities in a global setting.

• 
Gain broad exposure to Grundfos’ global operations while sharpening your consulting, project management, and leadership skills.

• 
Your background:

We are searching for an experienced professional who brings both strategic insight and operational execution capability yet still have a strong ambition to grow. We envision you have:

• 
A strong academic record (Master’s level preferred).

• 
6+ years of relevant experience, ideally with a background from management consulting or corporate strategy roles. M&A experience (Pre-DD & CDD) is a pre-requisite (significant M&A experience is a plus).

• 
A proven ability to lead complex projects involving multiple workstreams and stakeholders across business functions.

• 
A growth-oriented mindset with a demonstrated ability to learn quickly, adapt to new challenges, and lead change.

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with excellent communication and interpersonal abilities to influence and collaborate effectively across cultural and organisational boundaries.

• 
Excellent communication and stakeholder mgmt. skills, with a track record of previous exposure to top management.

Do you want to learn more?

If you have questions or would like to know more about this position, please contact Hiring Manager Kalindi Rana, Director, Strategic Growth Platforms, at krana@grundfos.com .

We look forward to hearing from you.

About Grundfos

Grundfos is one of the world’s leading water technology companies with more than 19.000 employees in 60+ countries all over the world. Our skills commit us to pioneering solutions to the world’s water and climate challenges and improve the quality of life for people. We dare to do things that others cannot or dare not do, as we believe innovation is not only a business opportunity, but an obligation. And what really matters to us is not short term profit, but the impact we make. By becoming part of our united powerful team, you too can drive this change no matter your role.

An inclusive team

We believe that the key to a work environment, where employees thrive and grow, is our ability to celebrate and value our differences in background, experiences and perspectives. In our recruitment process we welcome all professional people without consideration of age, colour, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental disability, ethnicity or religion.

Are you passionate about advancing electronic manufacturing processes and making pump technology smarter and more efficient? Then join our mission to pioneer smarter water solutions that reduce energy use and improve lives.

As our new Manufacturing Process Engineer, you'll be spearheading manufacturing engineering tasks in our Electronic Control Box production area that drives the intelligence and responsiveness of next-generation pump solutions. You'll be part of a diverse, supportive and inclusive culture, that celebrates our differences and puts people first by fostering growth, well-being, and a sense of belonging.

What you will be doing

As a key part of the Electronic Control Box Manufacturing team, you'll create impact by optimizing production processes and driving continuous improvements that enhance quality, speed, and overall equipment effectiveness across our component factory.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Drive production area performance by ensuring KPI targets for quality, speed, OPR, and OEE are consistently met

• Optimize manufacturing processes by collecting, monitoring, and acting on process data to improve cycle times, routings, and costing

• Solve daily production technical challenges and provide efficient support to keep operations running smoothly

• Manage VPC activities and follow up on production line testing after changes and maintenance

• Create investment reports and participate in the New Equipment Process for production line upgrades

• Participate in improvement workshops using Kaizen and value stream mapping methodologies

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you're a data-driven and systematic production engineering professional with strong collaboration skills and the ability to communicate effectively across professional groups. We'd also imagine that you are/have:

• Degree in Electronics Engineering, Production Engineering, or a related technical field

• Deep knowledge of production technical processes, ideally within electronic component manufacturing

• Experience with leading small projects and implementing process improvements

• Fluent in both Danish and English, orally and in writing

It's a plus if you also:

• Experience with Lean methodologies such as Kaizen and value stream mapping

• Familiarity with OPR/OEE metrics and production performance optimization

• Knowledge of compliance standards and regulations in electronic manufacturing

Why you'll love working here

Day to day, you can look forward to:

• A working environment built around your needs, with flexible hours, home working opportunities and parental support.

• Annual bonuses, health insurance and a strong focus on well-being activities.

• Three days' additional paid leave for volunteering.

• On-demand training and structured development programmes to support your growth.

Valuing our differences helps us see possibilities where others can't. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all abilities, experiences, and backgrounds. As part of our commitment to a safe and compliant hiring process, final candidates may be required to undergo a background check, subject to applicable local laws and regulations.

The Business Analyst – Investment Governance & Performance plays a pivotal role in shaping our global retail footprint. In this role you will be responsible for optimizing and controlling all Pandora’s investments in store leases, acquisitions and other network actions. By owning and driving best practices in investment evaluation, you will help support the strategic growth and profitability through data-driven decision-making on our global store network.

You will work closely with the Franchise & Network Management Team as well as local property and network teams, delivering high-quality analysis and recommendations to drive strategic initiatives such as store openings, closures, relocations, Forward Integrations and lease renewals.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• 
Evaluate and Review Investment Proposals.

• 
Ensure the accuracy and completeness of all submitted investment proposals (IPs).

• 
Validate compliance with accounting standards, including IFRS16 regulations.

• 
Assess business cases for financial impact and strategic alignment.

• 
Share approved IPs with the CCO/CEO/CFO for final sign-off.

• 
Track, Report and Analyse Investments.

• 
Maintain and update the global investment overview.

• 
Report and review the investment proposals vs actual performance in the hindsight report to measure accuracy.

• 
Deliver insights to enhance the accuracy of future investment decisions.

• 
Lead Bi-Weekly Investment Review Meetings

• 
Coordinate and host approval meetings with the Global Network & Franchise management team.

• 
Present investment proposals from market clusters for review and global approval.

• 
Develop and Improve Internal Tools and Processes

• 
Continuously improve reports, presentations and templates to reflect the strategic priorities and regulatory requirements.

• 
Promote and implement global best practices across clusters.

• 
Cross-Functional Collaboration

• 
Act as a trusted advisor to Global Network & Franchise management, Global Finance, Cluster Property and Cluster finance teams.

• 
Provide analytical support and challenge local teams to ensure business cases are both realistic and profitable.

**Your team

**The Global Network Development & Insights function partners with the Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) organization to provide strategic insights that shape Pandora’s global retail and franchise network. The team collaborates closely with Cluster Finance Directors and General Managers to drive performance, ensure retail excellence, and execute on global priorities.

You will report to the Network Expansion & Investments Senior Manager and join a high-impact team focused on data-led strategy and investment optimization.

**What We’re Looking For

**We are looking for a proactive and analytical team player with a strong business acumen and a critical mindset. You have a talent for transforming data into insights and a passion for driving performance through collaboration and strategic thinking.

**Your Qualifications Include

**

• A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.

• Minimum 2 years of experience in a similar role; experience in retail, real estate, fashion or FMCG is a plus.

• Proven ability to deliver insights through reports, dashboards, and presentations.

• Strong stakeholder management skills, including experience communicating with senior leadership.

• Proficiency in MS Excel; experience with Power Automate and Power BI/Query is a strong advantage.

**AI & Automation/Optimization

**We expect our future colleague to actively embrace the evolving role of AI and automation in business analysis. This means leveraging AI-powered tools to streamline investment evaluation workflows and enhance reporting accuracy.

**Additional Information

**Global Career Band: 5B

Start date: Ideally, January 1, 2027

**Did we get your attention?

**We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you would like to become part of Pandora's future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site at Pandora Group.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable **and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.****About Pandora

**Pandora is the world’s largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores. Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.description:
About Octarine

Octarine Bio is a Copenhagen-based biotech company making safe, sustainable, bio-based pigments. Our PurePalette™ platform uses precision fermentation and renewable raw materials to produce colourants that can replace petrochemical and mined pigments.

We are a team of around 15 people, working across pigment manufacturing, formulation and application development, and commercial development. As our pigment manufacturing processes reach full commercial scale, and our first pigment products are now in the hands of customers and partners, we are looking for someone with deep domain expertise in one or more of our core application areas (dyeing, printing, coatings and plastics) to make PurePalette™ work in real industrial applications and turn successful customer trials into lasting commercial products.

The role

You will be the technical owner of the PurePalette™ product range and the link between our lab and our customers. You will translate what the market needs into clear performance targets, work with our scientists to meet them, and make sure our pigment products perform once they reach a customer's processes.

We are looking for an applications expert in inks and coatings, plastics, or both, or in a closely related pigment application field. The title and scope will match your experience:

• Technical Product Specialist if you are earlier in your career and want a role with a lot of room to grow as the company scales.

• Head of Product Development if you have the experience to lead the product and applications function, shape the product roadmap and build a team.

In both cases you will report directly to our Chief Scientific Officer and work closely with our commercial team.

What you will do

Own the product, technically

• Be the technical expert for all PurePalette™ products and the first point of contact for technical questions from customers, partners and colleagues.

• Define the performance and quality parameters customers expect in each application, such as colour strength, dispersibility, heat stability, light and weather fastness, migration, rheology, and wash and rub fastness.

• Plan and coordinate the internal and external testing needed to prove each parameter, and turn the results into clear data packages for customers.

• Own, write and maintain our technical and product documentation, including Safety Data Sheets (SDS), Technical Data Sheets (TDS), Certificates of Analysis (CoA), product specifications and application guides.

Make our pigments work for customers

• Work with customers, distributors and partners to implement PurePalette™ products in their processes, from first lab trial to production run.

• Own the technical side of our partnerships with masterbatchers, ink manufacturers, dyehouses and research institutes. Set up project plans, manage technology transfer between parties, and troubleshoot problems until the product works in the target application.

• Handle technical customer feedback and complaints, find the root cause and feed lessons back into product and process development.

Decide what to develop next

• Identify where bio-based pigments offer real value to end users, and where they can genuinely meet customers' performance expectations.

• Work with Octarine scientists to map which applications our current pigments suit, and which applications we should target with future products.

• Work with our formulation and application scientists to refine formulations (dispersions, masterbatches, inks, dye and print pastes) to meet customer requirements.

• Work with our R&D and process teams to develop and implement strategies that improve pigment performance, for example through stabilisation, surface treatment or particle engineering.

• Benchmark our products against incumbent pigments and competing bio-based alternatives.

Connect technical and commercial

• Act as the bridge between Octarine's technical and commercial teams, translating customer needs into technical requirements and technical results into customer value.

• Join customer meetings, site visits and trade fairs as the technical voice of the company.

• Contribute technical content to sales materials, grant applications and investor discussions, and help capture new inventions for our IP portfolio.

What you bring

Pigment applications are many markets, not one. Printing inks alone span flexo, gravure, offset, screen and digital printing, and each places different demands on a pigment. The end markets differ just as much, from packaging and textiles to toys, consumer goods and coatings, each with its own performance, safety and regulatory requirements.

We need someone who knows this landscape in depth. You should understand the technical and performance requirements of each sub-application and market, judge where our pigments have a realistic and valuable fit, and work with our scientists to develop products that meet those requirements.

Specifically, we are looking for:

• An MSc or PhD in chemistry, polymer or materials science, chemical engineering, colour science or a related field, or equivalent industrial experience.

• Hands-on industrial experience applying pigments or colourants in textiles, inks and coatings, plastics and masterbatch, or a closely related field. For the Head of Product Development level, we expect around 5 or more years, including leading projects or people.

• A practical understanding of pigment dispersion and of how pigment properties such as particle size, surface chemistry and thermal stability affect performance in the final product.

• Experience with colour measurement (spectrophotometry, CIELAB, ΔE) and with standard ISO, EN or ASTM test methods for pigment and application performance.

• Experience writing or maintaining SDS, TDS and CoA documents, and working knowledge of REACH and CLP.

• Experience working directly with customers or external partners on trials, scale-up or technology transfer.

• The ability to explain technical results clearly to scientists, customers and commercial colleagues.

• A structured, self-driven way of working, and comfort with the pace and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• The confidence to take full ownership of the role from day one. You will set your own priorities, make decisions within your remit and drive projects to completion without close supervision, keeping the CSO informed rather than waiting for direction.

Nice to have

• Experience in both inks and coatings and plastics.

• Experience with textile dyeing or printing.

• Experience with organic pigments, natural colourants or other bio-based materials.

• Knowledge of food contact and product safety requirements, such as EU 10/2011, the Swiss Ordinance, EuPIA guidelines, EN 71-3 or ZDHC.

• Experience with quality systems such as ISO 9001, or with setting product specifications for a new product.

• An existing network in the European ink, coatings, masterbatch or textile industries.

What we offer

• A central role in bringing a new class of sustainable pigments to market, with real influence over which products we build and how.

• Direct work with the founding team and a short path from idea to decision.

• A small, highly skilled team of scientists across synthetic biology, fermentation, downstream processing, formulation and application.

• For earlier-career candidates, a role that can grow with the company. For senior candidates, the chance to build and lead the product function.

• Real autonomy and ownership of your work, and the chance to make a lasting impact at a fast-growing company developing new materials for industries that urgently need to change.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site is strongly preferred; hybrid working is possible for the right candidate.

Start date: As soon as possible

Reports to: Chief Scientific Officer

Employment: Full-time, permanent

Travel: Some travel to customers and partners within Europe

Right to work: Applicants must already have the right to live and work in Denmark. We are unfortunately not able to sponsor work visas at this time.

How to apply

Apply with your CV. Please highlight the pigment applications you have worked on and a technical problem you solved in a customer's process.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will fill the position as soon as we find the right person, so we encourage you to apply early.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are happy to answer questions about the role before you apply.

Sophion Bioscience is looking for an ambitious, customer-focused Vice President of Research & Development to lead and further develop our R&D organization.

This is a central leadership role with responsibility for Sophion’s technology strategy, product development execution, engineering capabilities, and R&D organization. You will ensure that priorities, resources, budgets, and development activities are managed with clarity and discipline, enabling us to deliver high-quality products that create measurable value for customers.

You will report to the CEO and as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute to Sophion’s overall direction and continued growth.

About the role

As VP R&D, you will lead and develop Sophion’s multidisciplinary R&D organization, setting a clear direction and creating the structure, leadership, and ways of working needed to deliver on our ambitions.

You will translate product and portfolio priorities into clear R&D priorities, roadmaps, and resource commitments, ensuring alignment and accountability across the organization. Working closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management, you will ensure R&D brings strong judgment and execution discipline to the development of differentiated and commercially successful products.

A key part of your mandate will be to strengthen the R&D organization and its leadership. You will develop leaders, build effective teams, establish clear governance and decision-making, and create a culture of collaboration, ownership, and delivery.

You will attract, develop, and retain talented people and ensure that R&D continues to grow in capability, maturity, and performance.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ on a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Set and execute Sophion’s R&D and technology strategy in alignment with the company’s overall direction and priorities.

• Lead and develop the R&D organization, including its structure, leadership capabilities, ways of working, and competencies.

• Clearly communicate R&D priorities, progress, risks, and trade-offs across Sophion and to the Leadership Team and Board.

• Own the R&D budget and ensure resources are allocated to the activities that create the greatest strategic and customer value.

• Drive portfolio and resource management, translating product priorities into actionable development roadmaps and execution commitments while balancing short- and long-term priorities.

• Ensure customer needs inform development decisions by driving broad R&D engagement with the market, key opinion leaders, and key accounts.

• Strengthen development governance, decision-making, accountability, milestones, KPIs, and transparent reporting.

• Drive continuous improvement in product quality, performance, reliability, and maintainability.

• Work closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management to assess opportunities and convert agreed priorities into robust and commercially viable products.

• Maintain appropriate quality and compliance standards across R&D activities.

• Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Who You Are

You are a strategic and hands-on R&D leader who can turn complex scientific and technical opportunities into high-quality products.

You bring clarity to complex situations and combine strong judgment with disciplined execution. You build strong teams, set clear priorities, use resources effectively, and deliver commitments.

You are engaging and decisive, and you build trust through transparency, communication, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. You are comfortable moving between strategic questions and operational details without losing sight of R&D and company priorities.

We expect that you:

• Master’s degree in science, engineering, technology, or a related field.

• Proven R&D leadership experience in complex, multidisciplinary product development, leading leaders and sizeable teams of specialized engineers and scientists across hardware, software, firmware & bioscience.

• Strong communicator with the ability to set the agenda, shape strategy, and communicate in a clear direction across the organization and with customers and investors.

• Track record of taking products from concept to successful global market use.

• Experience from life science tools, diagnostics, MedTech, laboratory instrumentation, or similar quality-critical environments is preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to improve execution, prioritization, organizational capability, and product quality.

• Strong strategic, customer, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and deliver results.

• Strong interpersonal, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with professional English proficiency.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact Helene Fife on hef@Sophion.com

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant or outsourcing company.

**Deliver with focus. Scale with intent 🚀

**Are you a delivery leader who knows how to guide enterprise customers through complex set-ups without over-engineering the journey? Do you care deeply about building scalable, repeatable SaaS delivery rather than one-off custom projects?

At Performativ, we’re building the infrastructure layer for modern wealth management. As our Engagement Manager, you’ll lead the enterprise rollout of our SaaS platform helping customers onboard successfully through structured delivery, clear communication, and lightweight technical engagement.

This is not a professional services consulting role. You won’t be buried in endless customer-specific code or heavy customizations. Instead, you’ll work cross-functionally to help customers adopt our product the right way: cleanly, securely, and in line with platform best practices so they can scale on top of us, not around us.

**What You Will Do

**

• Own enterprise set-up programs end to end (kick-off through go-live and hyper-care) against an agreed plan and scope (Statement of Work).

• Enable customers to integrate Performativ via standard platform patterns (APIs, SSO, configuration) without custom buildouts, working with product and engineering to flag gaps early and advocate for scalable paths.

• Own plan, scope, and change control, keeping scope tied to contract and change visible and decided rather than quietly absorbed, and support the Technical Program Lead on requirements, design documents, and acceptance-criteria sign-off.

• Run customer communication, cadence, and governance with reporting that keeps meetings short, and manage risk, dependency, and issue tracking (including customer-side).

• Lead a clean handover to Customer Success at go-live or hyper-care exit, including train-the-trainer sessions and supporting materials.

• Represent the program in internal capacity and exception reviews, bringing requests the plan cannot absorb back as options rather than committing on the spot.

• Build repeatable playbooks, documentation, and artefacts that make the next program faster. You will be measured on this, not only on your own delivery.

**How You Will Work

**You will run multiple programs at once, in a delivery pod alongside the Technical Program Lead, Integration Engineers, Data Migration Specialists, and Product Engineers. None report to you. Rather you get things done through clarity and relationships, not authority. You will report to the COO. This is an in-office role based at our Copenhagen office.

**What We're Looking For

**

• 7+ years in program or engagement management, consulting, product management, or another delivery-facing role, with a track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end to end.

• Comfort being firm with customers on scope and timeline while keeping the relationship stronger for it.

• Any industry background welcome. Experience with enterprise customers (banks, asset managers, regulated industries), balancing urgency against long-term maintainability highly advantageous.

• Structured and highly organized, producing written plans, governance cadences, and reporting that stakeholders can act on.

• Broad technical literacy across enterprise SaaS delivery: API-based integrations, SSO and security configuration, and data migration and mapping, including enough SQL to read and question a mapping. You do not build the integration, but you understand it well enough to scope it, question it, and know when something does not add up.

• Ability to build working fluency in the customer's business domain fast: within 90 days, able to discuss topics such as advice and suitability workflows and customer reporting without a subject-matter expert in the room.

• ITIL Foundation, PMP or PRINCE2 Certification would be beneficial.

**

The Human-Centred Computing Section, Department of Computer Science, invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in Human-Computer Interaction.

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project
 Digital technologies increasingly mediate how people experience, understand and respond to their bodies. The PhD project will investigate the relationship between bodies, technology and chronic illness, with a particular focus on self-tracking technologies. The project will explore how people with chronic conditions engage with these technologies and how technologies shape interactions with informal caregivers and health professionals. The project will critically examine how these technologies enact particular understandings of bodily difference and chronic illness, and how such understandings intersect with broader social, cultural and political norms. Within this topic, the PhD student will have some freedom to shape the focus of their work and the research questions they are interested in.

  The project will employ qualitative, participatory and design-oriented methods, with a particular emphasis on co-design and Research through Design. Co-design will involve working collaboratively with people with chronic conditions and other relevant stakeholders to explore their experiences of their bodies and technologies, and to imagine and develop new forms of technological interaction. Through Research through Design, the PhD researcher will develop and study experimental technological prototypes as a way of investigating alternative ways of sensing, representing and interacting with bodies. Design will be used not only to develop technological artefacts, but also as a means of generating knowledge about societal norms around chronic illness and the relationship between people and technology.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of human-computer interaction (HCI). The ideal candidate should have a strong background in user-centred research methods, with some experience of working in a research environment. We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in conducting design processes and developing both screen-based and physical computing prototypes. It is expected that candidates will have an M.Sc. degree in a relevant technical, design, or social science discipline. In addition, the ideal candidate will be able to document research capabilities (e.g., a thesis, publication, or project portfolio), have strong recommendations from supervisors and mentors, and possess a high level of intellectual humility. Preferred candidates would have advanced Danish language proficiency.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 The PhD fellow will become a member of the Human-Centered Computing (HCC) research section at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science. Here, we aim to fundamentally understand and improve the relation between computational technology and people. We are currently the top-ranked HCI research group in Europe (https://csrankings.org/#/index?chi&europe). Our research focuses on using computing to support people’s activities and well-being; inventing new ways for people to interact with technology, and understanding how human capabilities are influenced by technology. At the HCC section, we are currently over 15 faculty members, and over 20 postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and research assistants. We hold joint weekly research meetings, many annual retreats, and have a thriving social environment from daily lunches to larger events. We attend the most important international conferences, such as CHI. We particularly value having a supportive and collegial work environment that values and encourages diversity. 

  Copenhagen is a vibrant city, with many cultural offerings and easy access to the rest of Europe. For more information about working in Denmark, consult International Staff Mobility.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tariq Andersen, Department of Computer Science, tariq@di.ku.dk. The PhD project is led by Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, Department of Computer Science, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Computer Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 

  Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculy of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Computer Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY FOR POSITION below.

  Please include:

• Research Statement (max. one page excl. references) detailing your desired research focus. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research project within the topic of designing self-tracking technologies for chronic conditions you would wish to explore. This should include specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature and, if relevant, your previous research, and the potential impact and applications of this research. As we are interested in your own ideas and writing style, please do not use generative AI. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if relevant) 	
• Contact information for up to two people who have agreed to provide a reference.   Application deadline: 
 The deadline for applications is 29 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

jobs.occupation: DIAS Professor in Clinical Translational Psychiatry and Centre Leader for the Elite Centre for Clinical and Translational Psychiatry at Odense University Hospital and the University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS), the Department of Clinical Research at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and the Region of Southern Denmark seek an outstanding candidate to fill a fully tenured Professor position in the field of clinical translational psychiatry. The candidate is expected to start by agreement.

The candidate is expected to start by agreement.

We seek an exceptional researcher with demonstrated excellence in their discipline and a proven ability to push boundaries, challenge conventions, and engage in groundbreaking interdisciplinary research. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to cutting-edge advancements in their field while fostering collaboration across disciplines, embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven research. The ideal candidate will have a strong international research profile, an outstanding record of attracting competitive research funding, and a demonstrated ability to conduct interdisciplinary research. The successful candidate will be attached to the Department of Clinical Research, DIAS, and the Region, and must be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU and in the Region of Southern Denmark. 

What we offer

• 
The opportunity to lead a new elite centre for clinical and translational psychiatry, with five-year funding of DKK 17 million (equivalent to Euro 2.3 million), with the potential for a five-year extension.

• 
A strong interdisciplinary research environment through DIAS, comprising leading academics across medicine, science, and the humanities, with the opportunity to collaborate with outstanding researchers across SDU’s five faculties.

• 
Access to state-of-the-art research facilities at the newly built Odense University Hospital (OUH), where psychiatry and somatic care are integrated to foster collaboration between these fields.

• 
Comprehensive research support services from DIAS and SDU, targeting prestigious funding such as DNRF, ERC, and grants from Danish private foundations.

• 
If recruited from abroad or from industry, the candidate will be eligible for a fast-track DKK 11 million  (equivalent to Euro 1.5 million ) Lundbeck Foundation Start-Up grant.

• 
Reduced teaching obligations compared to a standard professorship, allowing the candidate to focus on research and leadership within the elite centre.

Who we are looking for 

We are seeking a highly accomplished researcher with expertise in the field of clinical translational psychiatry, who is eager to engage in collaborative activities within the DIAS framework. 

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

• 
A record of internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Publications in high-level peer-reviewed academic journals and leading innovative research programmes in clinical psychiatry. 

• 
An ability to attract significant external funding to support independent and collaborative research initiatives.

• 
Engagement in the international academic society. 

• 
Extensive experience in building and leading multidisciplinary research teams that integrate basic and clinical sciences, with an emphasis on translational research spanning from laboratory findings to clinical trials.

• 
A research focus in areas such as child and adolescent psychiatry, clinical psychopharmacology, epidemiology, molecular neurobiology, substance use disorders, or serious mental illness.

• 
The ability to develop a translational research programme in one or more of the mentioned fields, with a focus on building cooperative, multidisciplinary teams that bridge basic science and the design and execution of early-phase clinical trials.

• 
A demonstrated commitment to mentorship, teaching, and leadership, fostering the next generation of researchers in interdisciplinary research environments.

• 
Experience at Full or Associate Professor level within relevant fields.

• 
Fluency in English

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, mentor DIAS fellows, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.  

The Department of Clinical Research

The Department of Clinical Research does translational research spanning from basic research to patient care, within both somatics and psychiatry. The interdisciplinary research aims to improve patient treatment, health, and well-being. Researchers at the institute often have joint appointments between clinic, research, and education, ensuring a strong academic foundation for the research at Odense University Hospital (OUH) and in psychiatry. The researchers at the Department of Clinical Research primarily consist of doctors, nurses, and other healthcare professionals with main employment at OUH.

The Centre for Clinical and Translational Psychiatry

The centre will be based at the new Odense University Hospital, which integrates psychiatric and somatic care to promote close collaboration between the fields. The hospital includes a state-of-the-art adult psychiatric department with around 600 employees, 142 single rooms, and specialized sections for joint somatic-psychiatric care, rehabilitation, telepsychiatry, and more. The child and adolescent psychiatric department cover the entire region with about 600 employees, two inpatient wards with a total of 34 beds, and outpatient clinics at four geographical sites.

The centre’s aim is to advance novel psychiatric research through innovative approaches that will significantly impact future patient care. This includes translating discoveries from the laboratory to clinical settings, whether within narrow clinical fields or through broader cross-disciplinary collaborations that involve various clinical functions, professions, and institutions.

Additional information

For further information about being a professor at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk 

For further information and questions about the position, please contact the Head of the Department of Clinical Research Rikke Leth-Larsen at +456550 3477 or via email at rllarsen@health.sdu.dk or Medical Director Bjarne Dahler-Eriksen, Odense University Hospital, at +4523284068 or via email at bde@rsyd.dk. You may also contact the Vice Dean for Research and Innovation at the Faculty of Health Sciences, SDU, Uffe Holmskov at +45 6550 3775 or via email at uholmskov@health.sdu.dk regarding the position.

Application, salary, and employment terms

This position will be attached to the Department of Clinical Research in Odense. The successful candidate will be expected to regularly engage in DIAS activities and interdisciplinary cooperation in Odense. 

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

For more details on salary and taxation, please refer to the provided links about salary and taxation.

Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Application requirements

Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply now" link provided below.

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

The application must include the following:

• 
A motivation letter.

• 
A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contacts for possible references.

• 
Copies of relevant certificates/diplomas.

• 
A teaching portfolio detailing previous teaching experience.

• 
A complete list of publications, highlighting those most relevant to the position.

• 
Up to ten of the most relevant publications

• 
A research and publication plan for the next five years, including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

Submission guidelines

• 
Files must be submitted in PDF format, with each file no larger than 10 MB.

• 
If multiple files are needed for a single section, combine them into one PDF file.

• 
Zip files, image files (jpg, png, etc.), and password-protected PDF files will not be accepted. All PDF files must be unlocked to allow binding.

• 
The application deadline is February 7, 2027, at 23:59 CET. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Applications that are incomplete with regards to the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed by the committee. Shortlisting and tests may be used in the recruitment process and references may be obtained.  

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit the websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you will find information and facts about moving to, working, and living in Denmark.

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the recruitment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.  

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns themselves.

About SDU

SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.

SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

Equal opportunity employment

The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. 

SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to several security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.
